trial_court: Court of MM-02, Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (CT. CASES No. 320/2017)
case_name: Ramesh Bhatia vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr — Respondents

facts_of_case: Petitioner's cheque bounced; respondent filed complaint under Section 138 N.I. Act; parties entered into MoU to settle debt; petitioner seeks quashing of proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the complainant to prove that the cheque was dishonoured due to the drawer's default and not due to any other reasons.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted by Mr Sahani, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that the respondent No.2 had filed the criminal complaint under Section 138 N.I. Act against the petitioner for dishonor of cheque.
use_in: criminal cases under Negotiable Instruments Act

legal_principles.principle: A settlement agreement can be a valid defence to a cheque bounce complaint.
legal_principles.held: Out of these 25 Post Dated Cheques of Rs. 20,000/- each, some of the cheques have bounced and respondent No.2 has also initiated three more criminal complaints.
use_in: criminal cases under Negotiable Instruments Act

outcome.final_order: Application stands disposed of, subject to all just exceptions.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing criminal proceedings
representing clients in criminal complaints under section 138
